**Code-conventions review (`--review-pr`): `ad90ff097...HEAD` (billing webhook receiver auth, 15 files, +770/−1)**

I generated the full checklist of 57 rules and went through every item. I wrote it to the scratchpad instead of the repo, so no tracked files changed. I didn't run tests, lint or `gh`. I didn't need the review-learning lookup for any rule.

Rules that applied: CHANGE-01, PR-01, PR-02, MOD-01, MOD-03, MOD-04, MOD-06, NAME-01, REUSE-01, STYLE-01, TYPE-02, TYPE-03, TYPE-06, AUTH-03, ROUTE-01, CONFIG-01, CONFIG-02, CONFIG-05, TEST-01, TEST-02, TEST-04, TEST-08, LOG-01, LOG-04, SEC-02. The rest cover areas this diff doesn't touch (DB, cache, spaces, redirects, resilience, aggregates).

## Findings

| # | Rule | Severity | Location | Finding |
|---|------|----------|----------|---------|
| 1 | PR-02, PR-01, CHANGE-01 | Medium | `src/modules/billing/domain/billing-auth.service.ts:29` (also `:92-135`) | The doc comment says `mint` is "Used by the provisioning CLI (`scripts/generate-token.ts`)", but that file isn't in the repo or the diff. As shipped, only tests call `static mint`, so the docs don't match behaviour and the production code has no real caller. Either add the script in this PR, or move `mint` (and the comment) into the follow-up that adds the CLI. |
| 2 | MOD-04, MOD-03 | Medium | `src/datasources/jwt/jwt.module.ts:10`, used at `billing-auth.service.ts:7,125` | `jwtClientFactory` was module-private and is now exported so a domain service can call the raw jsonwebtoken client directly, skipping the `IJwtService` DI boundary. The only reason is the static, app-less `mint`. `JwtService.sign` already accepts `secretOrPrivateKey` and `algorithm`. Keep the factory private and put the CLI signing path in the script (or a small helper there), not in the injectable service. |
| 3 | TEST-02 | Medium | `src/modules/billing/routes/guards/billing-webhook-auth.guard.integration.spec.ts:113-176` | The integration spec starts Nest for every rejection case: HS256, wrong issuer, wrong audience, expired, not a service token, untrusted key. The last two repeat the unit tests at `billing-auth.service.spec.ts:138-170`. TEST-02 says integration/e2e should prove wiring once per route, with one representative 401 smoke test. Move the claim negatives (iss, aud, exp, algorithm) to `BillingAuthService` unit tests and keep the guard spec to: guard applied, no or non-Bearer header, one bad token → 401, one valid → 202. |
| 4 | LOG-04, REUSE-01 | Low | `src/modules/billing/domain/billing-auth.service.ts:82-86` | It narrows `error` by hand (`error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'unknown error'`). The repo convention is `asError` from `@/logging/utils` (see `oidc-auth.controller.ts:203`). |
| 5 | CONFIG-02 | Low | `src/config/entities/schemas/configuration.schema.ts:54` | `BILLING_WEBHOOK_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY` is `z.string().optional()` with no link to `FF_BILLING_WEBHOOK`. The only fail-fast check is `getOrThrow` in the service constructor (`billing-auth.service.ts:49-50`). The schema already has a `requiredWhen` superRefine pattern (e.g. `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` when `FF_SES_EMAIL`, lines 196-216). Add the public key there with `requiredWhen: FF_BILLING_WEBHOOK === 'true'` so bad config fails during schema validation. |
| 6 | NAME-01, STYLE-01 | Low | `src/modules/billing/domain/billing-auth.service.ts:108` | `24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000` is an inline magic multiplier, and the trailing comment `// (now + days × 24h)` just repeats the code. Pull it out as a named constant (e.g. `MS_PER_DAY`) and drop the comment. |
| 7 | MOD-04 | Low | `src/modules/billing/domain/billing-auth.service.ts:21` | `DEFAULT_BILLING_SERVICE_TOKEN_SUBJECT` is exported but only used in the same file (line 105). Make it module-local. |
| 8 | NAME-01 | Low | `src/modules/billing/routes/guards/billing-webhook-auth.guard.ts:21` | The injected `BillingAuthService` is named `tokenService`. It should be `billingAuthService` so the name matches the dependency. |

No findings for the auth/crypto choice (it reuses the existing `IJwtService`, the algorithm is pinned to ES256, and the HS256 downgrade is tested). Also clean: the feature-flag gating in `AppModule` (MOD-01), the `.env.sample.json` entries (CONFIG-05), the SPDX headers, the unit spec building the service directly with `new` (TEST-01), and warn-level logging for rejected tokens (LOG-01).

**Unresolved:** #1 and #2 are linked. Whether `mint` belongs in this PR depends on whether the provisioning CLI is coming in a follow-up. That's a call for the PR author.
